title: Most of the Great Wall Isn't Brick - It's Rammed Earth | China Travel Expert
description:
Most of the Great Wall isn't brick - it's rammed earth.

The famous grey brick-and-stone wall near Beijing is the exception, not the rule. For more than 2,000 years, most of the Great Wall was built by packing earth between wooden boards and tamping it down one thin layer at a time (hangtu). In the desert, builders layered in reeds and tamarisk branches for strength. Only the Ming faced long stretches in brick and stone - mostly the sections near Beijing. Of about 21,196 km of wall recorded in China's 2012 survey, the brick-and-stone Ming wall is only about 8,852 km.

🧭 Expert Tip: For the postcard brick wall, visit a Ming section near Beijing (Mutianyu or Jinshanling); to see the original rammed earth, head west to the Han wall near Dunhuang.
